1919723446767956352.content:
Jason, let’s break down your "largest tax hike in history" drama with some actual history. The TCJA cut the top rate from 39.6% to 37%—a temporary break set to expire in 2025. Letting it lapse isn’t a hike; it’s a return to 2016 levels. If you want a real tax hike, look at 1993: Clinton raised the top rate from 31% to 39.6%, an 8.6% jump. Or 1942, when the top rate went from 81% to 88% to fund a war. Your 2.6% bump doesn’t even make the podium. And this "one big beautiful bill"? It’s a Trump slogan, not a policy. The TCJA was sold as a middle-class miracle, but the numbers tell a different story: in 2018, the top 5% of households got 40% of the individual cuts, per the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities. Meanwhile, the standard deduction doubled, but axing personal exemptions clawed back most gains for families. The real winners were the ultra-rich, not the middle class you’re pretending to champion.

Now, about those family farmers and small businesses you’re so worried about—let’s get real. The TCJA’s pass-through deduction was a boon for high-earning professionals like doctors and lawyers, not rural farmers. Only 2.6% of farm households even paid estate taxes before the TCJA, per USDA data. Most farmers saw little relief, while urban elites cashed in. And small businesses? Many are pass-through entities, sure, but the biggest benefits went to the top earners, not mom-and-pop shops. Your bill’s "certainty" sounds more like a certainty of more tax breaks for the wealthy while the rest of us pick up the tab. Try again, Jason.

His style is informal and exasperated, using exclamations, rhetorical questions, tags, hashtags, links, and softened profanity such as schitt.
